title: Did you know… Saul approved of persecution before becoming Paul?
paragraphs: Did you know… Saul approved of persecution before becoming Paul?

He didn’t just “have a past.”
He approved murder.

Before he became Paul…
he stood there.
Watching.
Agreeing.
Nodding.

Saul of Tarsus wasn’t neutral.
He was in on it.

Acts 8:1 says he approved the killing of Stephen.
Not forced.
Not confused.
He wanted it.
And it didn’t stop there.

He hunted believers.
Dragged them out.
Tore families apart in the name of “righteousness.”

Religious.
Passionate.
Dead wrong.
But here’s what we miss…

God didn’t cancel Saul.
God confronted him.

On the road to Damascus—
light broke through.
A voice cut deep:
“Why are you persecuting Me?” (Acts 9:4)
Not “them.”
Me.
Jesus took it personally.

And in that moment, the persecutor collapsed…
and a preacher was born.
This is the scandal of grace:

The man who tried to destroy the Church
became the man who helped build it.

The hands that once arrested believers
would later write letters that still set captives free.

Romans.
Ephesians.
Philippians.
Scripture.
Some scholars interpret Paul’s transformation as the most dramatic conversion recorded in the New Testament. And it is.
Because it crushes every excuse we cling to.

“Too sinful.”
“Too far gone.”
“Too late for me.”
No.

If Jesus can rewrite Saul…
He can rewrite you.
Listen carefully:

Your worst chapter
is not your final verse.

The same grace that stopped Saul
is calling your name.

Not to shame you—
but to save you.

Not to expose you—
but to redeem you.
Turn.
Right now.

Lay it down.
The pride.
The secret sin.
The past you think disqualifies you.

Jesus already paid for it at the cross.
He didn’t die for a better version of you.
He died for the real one.

And He rises to give you a new name,
a new path,
a new purpose.
Because they haven’t.
